label: UniFi Express 7
description: UniFi Express 7 (UX7) - 1x 2.5G RJ45 (2.5G/1G/100M/10M) + 1x 10G RJ45 (10G/5G/2.5G/1G/100M) that is the default WAN; WiFi 6/6E + 7 on 6/5/2.4 GHz; 22 W max, USB-C powered.
notes:
Read 2026-11-19 from https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/ux7 (HTTP 200, 688,360 B, title "UniFi Express 7 - Tech Specs"): "Port Layout - 2.5 GbE RJ45 1 (2.5G/1G/100M/10M) / 10 GbE RJ45 1 (10G/5G/2.5G/1G/100M)", "Default WAN Ports (1) 10 GbE RJ45", "Max. WAN Port Count 1", "Max. Power Consumption 22W", "Power Method USB type C (5V DC/5A)". Routing/firewall rows used for the capability list: "Stateful Firewall", "Advanced NAT (SNAT / DNAT / Masquerade / NAT Pooling / 1-to-1 NAT)", "Customizable DHCP Server", "Dynamic Routing - OSPF", "VLAN/Subnet-based Traffic Segmentation" - all ticked. Radio rates from "Throughput": 6 GHz 5.7 Gbps, 5 GHz 4.3 Gbps, 2.4 GHz 688 Mbps, one 2x2 radio per band. Category is router, not wireless: Ubiquiti files the SKU under Cloud Gateways (the tech-spec path itself) and its BSSID row reads "4 per Radio (Gateway Mode) / 4 per Radio (AP Mode)"; the store page (https://store.ui.com/us/en/products/ux7, HTTP 200, 587,404 B) calls it a "super-compact 10G Cloud Gateway with integrated 6 GHz WiFi 7". The default WAN port is documented in prose rather than as a role on eth1 so no saved lab changes which port it treats as uplink. No datasheet is published for this SKU - the tech-spec page lists only the quick-start (https://dl.ui.com/qig/ux7, which serves an HTML viewer, not a PDF with a text layer).
Power: none of these copper ports accepts PoE. Vendor page https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/ux7 (HTTP 200, 688,360 B, read 2026-11-19, server-rendered tech-spec table) says "Power Method = USB type C (5V DC/5A)"; a box fed from mains, a USB-C supply or a DC jack has no PoE-PD front end, so eth0 / eth1 now declare poeIn: false. Without that declaration the engine's isPoePd() match on "unifi" gave each silent copper port a 12.95 W 802.3af draw - the defect PR #2118 and PR #2121 fixed across the UXG family (refs #130).

WAN/LAN role separation, read 2026-11-21. The vendor numbers the sockets and names the uplink. Ubiquiti's controller device database (`https://static.ui.com/fingerprint/ui/public.json`, HTTP 200, 832,585 B, `devices` entry with `sku` = UX7) prints `ports` = {"eth0": "LAN", "eth1": "WAN"} with `switchPorts` absent and `numberOfPorts` 2; the product page prints the same split in words - `Default WAN Ports (1) 10 GbE RJ45`, `Max. WAN Port Count 1` - at https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/cloud-gateways/ux7 (HTTP 200, 688,360 B). `role` is the field `engine/device.js` `ownsIpOn` reads (`owner.role && inIface.role && owner.role !== inIface.role`, "WAN and LAN are separate L3 surfaces ... role separation outranks the VLAN shortcut") and it fires only when BOTH sides carry one, so a LAN bank with no role leaves the invariant false: with 192.168.1.1/24 on `eth0`, `ownsIpOn(eth1, '192.168.1.1')` returned true, and a host cabled to `eth1` inside that subnet was answered by the LAN gateway. `eth1` now declares role "wan" and `eth0` "lan"; measured after the change, `eth1` no longer owns the LAN address, `eth0` still owns its address, and `eth1` still answers its own. The vendor's `Max. WAN Port Count 1` is a ceiling with no per-socket assignment, so no port here claims `dualRole`: a lab that needs a second WAN still has to be told which socket the firmware gives up.
